steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: Are you moving or not?!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Are you moving or not?!

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: NO!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Wh-What a passionate debate! I can feel the heroic blood in their voices!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: ...But they're not actually saying anything.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: They're just yelling at the top of their lungs. I don't even know what they're saying.

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: The dispute over Athenius's route has been brewing between the fruit farmers and the temple builders for ages.

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Embarrassing, really, to make a random tourist off the street try to solve our dispute. Heck, even I couldn't tell half of what they're saying...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: You said you wanted to know what they're saying...

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Stop looking for trouble, Titi.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: This 'random tourist off the street' has an idea.

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Hey! Don't just wander in there! Things could get rough!

The craftsmen rep and the militiaman arguing on behalf of the fruit farmers are not budging in the slightest, their faces red with anger. They fail to notice the pair of pointy black ears poking out from beneath the stone table.
The tiny Feline girl leaps out and grabs their hands with a grin, bringing them together in a handshake.
Caught off guard, the two reps lose their balance and topple onto the stone table, staring at the jolly intruder.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Hey, who brought this girl to the temple? This is no place for children.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: See, you're so unreasonable, even an outlander is embarrassed. You're a disgrace to Athenius!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Stop adding fuel to the fire!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Listen, girl, this is Minoan business. We don't need some foreigner telling us how to make up.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Who said anything about making up?

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep & Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: Whuh?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The only way to solve a problem is to face it directly. How long do you think the peace would last, even if you made up here and now?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Besides, when in Minos, do as the Minoans do. The heroic epics and fantastical stories of Minos are full of ancient wisdom. You don't need me to tell you how to solve your problems.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: They say the mere mention of Heraces, the greatest Minoan warrior, sent enemies fleeing in terror.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But he never raised a hand against his fellow Minoans. If someone insulted him, he would challenge them to arm-wrestling.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Settle it with a contest of strength, eh? Sounds good! Spares us a sore throat.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I'm not done yet.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: There is another legend about a silent hero, who was once a bold and passionate youth, surrounded by flowers and adoration.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: As fate would have it, he learned a forbidden secret, knowledge that no one should possess, so he kept silent for thirty years.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Wait, we know the legend of Heraces, but who's this 'silent hero'? Did you just make him up on the spot?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Oh, it's a Minoan tale that my father used to tell me. It's rather obscure, but it's a really good parable—

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Ahem. Anyway, I propose that you follow in the footsteps of ancient Minoans, and settle this with an arm-wrestling match.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But with one extra condition—you only get to talk if you win, no matter how pissed you might be.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Never heard that rule before.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Are you poor with words, or weak of limb?

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Enough talk. Let's do it.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Alright! The inaugural First Temple Arm-Wrestling Tournament is on. Ready, set—

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Go!

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Well, well, well! The militiaman looks lean, but he's got skill, and he takes round one when the big guy loses focus for a second!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: Shut it! Loser doesn't get to talk!

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: New apples can't get out with all the stone piled up at the crossing! The orchards are all in the mountain's shadow, and the apples that haven't ripened yet don't get any sun! The whole harvest's going to the dumps at this rate!

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: One-nil. Round two.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Hey, all those muscles ain't for nothing! Looks like hauling marble is good exercise!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: We can't move the stone until the apples are out of the way! Besides, the building of the First Temple was inspired by the Minoan heroes! Who's gonna take responsibility if the work's delayed? You?

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: One-all. Next!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Apple harvesting and hauling stone... I see.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Minoans sure are fun to watch! But things will get less interesting when they start getting tired...

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Hey, why did they stop?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: They've realized the arm-wrestling isn't about determining a victor, but giving them an opportunity to hear each other out.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: When you're angry, your ears stop working, and even simple things become complicated, much less long-standing disputes.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: You're more thoughtful than you look.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: But how do you solve the core problem, now that you've gotten emotion out of the way?

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Looks like a draw.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Young lady...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Call me Titi.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: It's not like we screwed the fruit farmers on purpose, Titi.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: We've got a lot of hands in the rebuilding, but they only quarry stone when they please, where they please. I brought fifteen tons of marble down the mountain by myself yesterday, and it's still far from enough.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: Look, we understand. But the apples don't care.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Increasing quarrying efficiency, while getting enough sun for the apples... why don't we meet in the middle, then?

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Just remove the peak that's blocking the sunlight.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Hahahaha! Some 'middle'! That's the craziest thing I've ever heard!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: It is intriguing, though.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Out of personal curiosity, I studied the urban planning and natural environment of Athenius on my way here.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The peak that's in the way of the sunlight is only a secondary peak, with soft soil at the top and a large marble layer underneath—it would make an excellent quarry.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: You mean we can get sunlight to the orchards by leveling the peak, without having to change the city's route? Is that even possible?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The fruit farmers must join the quarriers.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Adding more hands is the quickest way to increase efficiency. We'll also need to get the craftsmen scattered across the mountains together.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: If you can carry fifteen tons of marble a day all by yourself...

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Then leveling the peak is not impossible.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: The rebuilding of the temple was the collective decision of the citizens of Athenius. We certainly won't complain, if we can solve the sunlight problem at the same time.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: I'll go talk to the farmers!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Problem solved!

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: All thanks to you, Titi.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Don't mention it.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It looks amazing, even in its incomplete state... Now, I'm even more curious about the one running this project.

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: Speaking of which, we still have a problem.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Craftsmen Rep
steps.text: The original proponent of the First Temple project, Pallas, went missing last night.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: '...Our joy was for both of us, but now eternal peace is yours alone.'

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: 'The breeze in the mountains of Heria and the rivers of the Agnes Plains shall shine in your eyes no more.'

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: 'Neither shall my heart know the tranquility of night and the leisure of day again...'

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It's been seven years, Ithakos, old friend.
The tall warrior places the cyclamen flowers before the white grave marker.
His movements are light and gentle, but several white petals still fall upon the ground.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You're late.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I'm simply passing through, on my way to a burdenbeast ranch with a view.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: You can find all the excuses you want, but you know you can't let it go.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Neither can I.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You haven't once visited the Endymion Temple in your five years in Athenius.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The first and last time you came was when you brought Ithakos's bloody chiton.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I don't need the guidance of the heroes.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: But you continue to dream the same dream. You blame yourself for sending Ithakos across the river, to the battle where he died.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The river runs only in my dreams now, since the Sargonians built a dam upstream.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It brought the melting snow from Heria's peaks to my homeland, and it brought him...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Ithakos was one of the few true friends that I had, one who was never concerned for who I am or what I can do.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: His family was tormented by the fires of war, and his father lived most of his life as a broken man. But he would not accept the same fate. His eyes were bright and eager when he received divine revelation.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Whatever the outcome, he found a friend and a brother in you. Did he ever visit you in your dreams, telling you not to mourn him anymore?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It's your place to interpret dreams, and mine to mourn and remember. I will soothe my rage in my own way.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The war is over. Sargon has signed a non-aggression pact with us, and this visit by the Sargonian mission is a symbol of our new relationship.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I know that. Lydia made a point to put me in my place.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The first Astynomos in Athenian history elected by popular vote, empowered to handle diplomatic matters and certain public issues independent of the council and the priests...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: She's caused you a fair share of trouble, hasn't she?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Endymion Temple has not been affected yet, but some fringe clerics and the roles of their temples are being marginalized. Besides...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Kereseira's First Temple is nearing completion. There should be a ceremonial play organized by the priests to call the spirit of Kereseira into the temple and grant Minos her protection.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Now, the play is being organized by the Astynomos' Office.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The Astynomos purported to assent when I discussed this matter with her a few days ago, but she was evasive when it came to the program we'd choose...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: To her, the priests and their ceremonies are just props to promote Minoan tourism.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Your insistence on using canonized classical drama will only be seen as an act of aggression by the priesthood.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I understand that reform is inevitable, but...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Some things will not and can not change.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Lydia's little power plays on the administrative side are none of my business, but I won't stand idly by if the Sargonian visitors have ill intent.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I'm no hero, just an ordinary Infected, and I don't need the guidance of divine revelation, but I still dream.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: If I tell you that I dreamt of a river running red with blood, as Ithakos did nine years ago...

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: How would you interpret it?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Xanthos!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Excuse me. I have work to do at the crossing, and an apprentice waiting for me.

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: You're really too kind, Titi. Not only did you solve our dispute with the fruit farmers, you're also helping us look for Pallas.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It's nothing. Besides, I want to meet the one who came up with the temple project, face-to-face.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: This Pallas was last seen at the crossing?

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: She was sitting on the docks, drinking and muttering in the direction of distant Mt. Hymnoi.

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: She's helped us with so many things since the rebuilding of the temple began. Although she doesn't hold any position in the temples of Athenius, and Kassandra from Endymion Temple is the one in charge of the responsibilities that are above-board...

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: Pallas was the one who took care of everything behind the scenes, from the division of labor to procurement to smoothing things over with the right people.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I see. It's certainly concerning that someone so reliable would go missing all of a sudden...

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: Ah, well... it's not the first time.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Almost forgot to ask. What does she look like?

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: A small Forte lady, always seems like she's half-asleep. She wears a little flower on her head.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: A little flower... the kind with two leaves, and petals so red you can't see the wrinkles?

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: Yes! How did you know?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Does it look like that?
The craftsman turns in the direction that Titi is pointing, to see a small red flower swaying gently in a pile of apples.

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: Yes, it does... but that's one of the apple farmers' crates, isn't it? What's a flower doing there?

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: Wait, there's something inside! Duck!
It is as though the crate has just woken up, sending ripe apples pouring across the docks, falling into the clear waters of the Delphi Canal.
A Forte slides out from the bed of fruit, rubbing her eyes at the sudden influx of bright sunlight.

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: P-Pallas?

steps.name: Craftsman
steps.text: Guys! Guys! No need for the boat! We found Pallas!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: This is Pallas, the people's hero, the proponent and reliable supervisor of the rebuilding plan?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: She's not quite what I imagined...
Titi approaches the young woman on the ground curiously.
She examines the horns for signs of battle, trying to determine her weapon's construction, whether it is able to support unique Originium Arts...
She even has the urge to reach for the mysterious little flower, to see if it is a boon from the Minoan heroes.
But Titi senses nothing unusual, except the sweet scent of apples.
The young woman seems to have woken up. Titi leans in to hear what she is muttering.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Mount... Hymnoi...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The western peak... level it... to let the sunlight...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Tell the farmers and workers... what's missing...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Yes... apple cider should be... shared...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Leveling the peak to solve the sunlight problem? So she came to the same conclusion I did... she's thinking about rebuilding the temple, even in her sleep.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Who says a hero has to be big and brawny? How could I forget that I'm in Minos, not Sargon?

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Mm... who are you?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: We meet at last, Pallas, first proponent of the rebuilding of Kereseira's First Temple.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I'm Medjehtiqedti Nasutu Mashayer, ambassador from Sargon.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Medj...?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: My friends call me Titi.
